lines: These files are public by design, so what gitleaks matches in them is not reported:
appinfo/signature.json, the integrity signature: 1,153 matches in what ships, 1,156 matches in 1 commit.

In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
vendor/google/apiclient-services/src/CloudAsset/ResourceSearchResult.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 4 matches in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/google/apiclient-services/src/Compute/CustomerEncryptionKey.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 2 matches in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/google/apiclient-services/src/DataManager/AwsWrappedKeyInfo.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
vendor/google/apiclient-services/src/DataManager/GcpWrappedKeyInfo.php, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in what ships (generic-api-key).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.
